issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Theorem 1, the variation of the action functional J with respect to delta phi yields the integral of the inner product of (Tv circ phi)^T pi + partial pi / partial t + grad V circ phi with delta phi. Setting this variation to zero by the fundamental theorem of the calculus of variations requires (Tv circ phi)^T pi + partial pi / partial t + grad V circ phi = 0, which implies partial pi / partial t = - (Tv circ phi)^T pi - grad V circ phi. Instead, the authors conclude with a plus sign: partial pi / partial t = - (Tv circ phi)^T pi + grad V circ phi. This sign discrepancy arises because the action functional J was defined with + V circ phi instead of - V circ phi (which is needed to match the - 1/2 <v,v> kinetic term in the Hamilton-Pontryagin framework).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the action functional J with - <V circ phi> instead of + <V circ phi> to properly reflect the Hamilton-Pontryagin formulation of the minimization problem (6). Its variation with respect to delta phi then gives - grad V circ phi in the inner product, which correctly solves to partial pi / partial t = - (Tv circ phi)^T pi + grad V circ phi in Theorem 1 and consistently yields (8) in Theorem 2.
issues.overall_effect: Equation (7) in Theorem 1 does not follow from the action functional J as defined. Consequently, Theorem 2 directly relies on this faulty equation in its proof to derive the modified Euler equation (8); with the actual critical curves of J as written, the resulting equation would have - grad(p + V) rather than - grad(p - V).
issues.title: Sign error in Euler-Lagrange optimality condition for costate and action functional
issues.why_classification: A standard local sign correction in the definition of the augmented action functional J completely resolves the derivation in Theorem 1 and preserves the stated results of both Theorem 1 and Theorem 2 without requiring new proof architecture or weakening any substantive claims.
